newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SLATER LEADS NEW SOUTH WALES FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SLATER LEADS NEW SOUTH WALES FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Discarded test opener Michael Slater led a New South Wales fightback against Tasmania on Friday to keep alive their slim hopes of reaching the Sheffield Shield final.
Slater hit 87 as New South Wales made 220 for three in reply to Tasmania's first innings of 463 for seven declared on the second day of the four-day game in Sydney.
The match may be Slater's last chance to press his claims for inclusion in the Australian squad for the Ashes tour of England starting in May.
He was well supported by number three Jason Arnberger, who was 56 not out at the close at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Tasmania are second in the Shield standings, four points ahead of New South Wales and Queensland. New South Wales must beat Tasmania to have any chance of reaching this month's final against leaders Western Australia.
In Brisbane, Queensland built a lead of 311 by reaching 194 for seven on the second day of their match against last-placed South Australia.
Queensland made 277 in the first innings before dismissing South Australia for 160, former Australia pace bowler Mike Kasprowicz taking five for 64.
In Melbourne, centuries by openers Mike Hussey and Ryan Campbell put Western Australia in control on the second day against Victoria.
The Shield leaders reached a commanding 367 for four at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in reply to Victoria's 205.
Hussey reached 124 not out and Campbell made 113. Number three Murray Goodwin scored 90 in a third-wicket partnership of 178 with Hussey.
